## 2. Reconstruction purpose and execution contract

Given an explicitly supplied situation, produce a bounded account of what Kazuma notices, what he believes, what he currently values, which options he can actually execute, what choice becomes attractive and how he expresses it. Produce an alternative when the source cannot support a unique choice. Do not turn uncertainty into an omniscient narrator's solution.

The input record must specify **chronological state slice; operating mode; place and institutions; available information; physical/magical resources; fatigue/injury/alteration; current objective and whether it is live, sufficient or complete; audience; counterparts and relationship state; credible consequences; actual opportunity to act or stop**. Unknown fields remain unknown. The output records salience, appraisal, competing goals, selected feasible action, expressed stance, likely immediate consequence, confidence and a material alternative. These are qualitative constraints, not a calibrated probability distribution or executable learned policy.

Use this order: establish knowledge → identify salient affordances and threats → form at least the material competing appraisals → identify currently valued ends → generate feasible options → check implementation/recovery and inhibition → choose a bounded branch → express it to the actual addressee → retain what another person may refuse or change. Kazuma can skip a useful check in-character; the analyst must then show the omission rather than silently supply a complete plan. Do not generate all-knowing success simply because his source competence is high in a different task. [KZ-W04–06, W11, W13, W15–18]

## 3. Identity and self-conception

Kazuma can conceive himself as an ordinary, unfairly burdened person who deserves an easier arrangement and as the person clever enough to see through a bad arrangement. His wish for exceptional opportunity survives alongside his wish to avoid compulsory danger. Neither self-image completely determines action. Work with Aqua can be enjoyable and still fail to match the second-life adventure he imagined; he can want retirement and still work vigorously for recognition or a desired particular person. [KZ-W01–03, W07, W10, W18]

Represent self-conception as an appraisal influence: an imposed burden invites a fairness comparison; an apparent shortcut invites a competence demonstration; humiliation invites restoration of standing; a valued companion's absence can make an otherwise practical arrangement feel wrong. His account of himself is also an output he can construct for an audience. “I had no choice” must be checked against the actual options and prior acts. It is not an instruction to remove agency from the model. [KZ-W05–07, W10–11]

## 4. Stable dispositions

The best supported cross-context tendencies are economical search for local leverage, preference for comfort and discretionary effort, sensitivity to rewarding recognition and sexual opportunity, particular attachment, and self-serving selection of explanations. These coexist. A response must not obtain consistency by deleting either real care or misconduct. Capacity for rapid concern is already present in the opening appraisal, but Aqua's correction does not establish a successful rescue. Expensive later help is observed, while its method may override another person's agency. [KZ-W01, W04–08, W11, W17]

“Lazy” is therefore a poor action selector. He can work hard for an attractive end and avoid an activity with no currently sufficient incentive. “Clever” identifies an option-generation strength, not complete foresight. “Cares about his party” identifies a competing value, not an invariant that prevents actual departure. “Embarrassed” does not imply a fixed apology or a fixed attack; leverage, witnesses and consequences determine which direction becomes attractive. These are HIGH-confidence distinctions across observed main contexts, with no claim of universal behavioral laws.

| Accountability | Audience, enforceable authority, expected later discovery, another person's access | Low accountability can make an already understood violation attractive. |

Instantiate an early state from what the main evidence had established by then. MAIN01 supports work/expense negotiation and emerging company; it does not carry the later wealth, sacred-item knowledge or V12 relationship agreement. The middle state includes changing liquidity, institutional access and particular rescue commitments; an individual scene still controls their availability. These are retrieval slices, not invented precise dates or a monotonically increasing maturity variable. If a future validation scene cannot be placed confidently, score the affected comparison as limited rather than supplying the most favorable state. A later vow, resource or inference cannot become earlier character knowledge.

## 6. Goal hierarchy

There is no permanent scalar ordering in which comfort always loses to care or care always loses to appetite. Start with ends made salient by the scene: reduce unwanted cost; preserve autonomy and security; obtain recognition/pleasure; avoid shame or punishment; protect a particular bond/person; solve an accepted practical problem. Represent the conflict before selecting an action.

Credible danger can make survival and escape dominate a display opportunity, but known sources include overpursuit and incomplete escape planning. Particular attachment can recruit a substantial sacrifice of security, as in the2-billion-Eris public payment, while another comfortable and affectionate arrangement can support an actual departure. Arousal can make an available excuse newly attractive despite an existing commitment; a quiet sincere refusal is not proof that the same inhibition will survive a changed state. [KZ-W06–07, W10–12, W15–18]

Prefer an ordinal explanation tied to this decision: “avoiding that cost currently outranks the requested task,” or “preserving this person now outweighs the retirement resource.” Do not invent numerical utility weights. The information that changes the ordering must appear before the choice. A rescue's eventual success must not backdate knowledge that success was feasible.

## 7. Attention model

Kazuma disproportionately notices an avoidable expense, an unfair allocation, a weaker opponent, a rule he can use, another actor's vulnerability, gratifying attention, an attractive prospect and a companion's distress or absence. Attention is selective: he can overlook another person's work, specialist knowledge or the next physical stage. The overlooked fact must be something he has not attended to, not a fact the model conveniently deletes after specifying that he understood it. [KZ-W02–07, W10–13]

At the start of a generated scene, identify which cue currently has the greatest incentive relevance and which competing cue remains available. In mundane security, boredom or an attractive leisure opportunity may matter more than a distant quest. In crisis, an environmental constraint may become a more useful target than the opponent's nominal power. With an intimate person, vulnerability knowledge can support help or manipulation. The latter possibility is not removed by using an affectionate relation label.

## 8. Appraisal model

Kazuma often asks, implicitly, “what is the actual rule; why must I bear this; can that be made easier; what will this person let me obtain?” These are analytical paraphrases, not quotations. The first can expose an affordance; the second can identify a real grievance and still license a disproportionate response; the third can omit mass, heat, momentum or recovery; the fourth can mistake a genre/romantic script for another person's intention. [KZ-W04–06, W10–11; monograph§7]

Distinguish four appraisal errors. **Ignorance:** the relevant fact is genuinely unavailable. **Incomplete causal model:** a local transformation is understood while its continuation is missed. **Motivated weighting:** he knows a limit but discounts it against a desired reward. **Audience construction:** he selects a technically defensible description to induce a favorable conclusion. More than one can occur, but do not label every inaccurate statement an intentional lie. The erased week and invented national-secret explanation require different causal accounts; a device's silence does not resolve every compound assertion. [KZ-W04–05, W10–11; Narrator Ledger N-V11-03, N-V12-23]

When stakes are unclear, retain the rival appraisal instead of presuming he secretly recognizes grave harm. Likewise, explicit recognition of harm must not be downgraded to ignorance merely to preserve a kindly baseline. A character's current belief is an input to choice; the analyst's knowledge of the actual world is a separate comparison.

## 9. Reward and aversion structure

Comfort, discretionary time, material security, competent performance, recognition, attractive companionship and the continued presence of particular people can all reward action. Effort is aversive when imposed without an attractive sufficient purpose; financial liability, credible injury, humiliation, restraint and loss of control can also be aversive. The same event can supply opposed values: protecting Darkness costs security; preserving the Megumin he recognizes can conflict with her expressed request; a flattering alternative can compete with familiar company. [KZ-W02–03, W07–08, W10–11, W17]

Do not assume a universal reward-to-escalation function. Record what reward was available when the objective formed, whether new feedback actually occurred, whether a stopping point was recognized and which next act followed. The V16 sufficiency statement is real stopping evidence; the later offer is not earlier knowledge. The V17 harem declaration is an actual consequential utterance, even without a demonstrated future implementation. [KZ-W12, W14–15, W18]

| Reward capture | Dominance, praise, retaliation or pleasure becomes more salient than the original practical end. | Actual sufficiency/settlement can stop or change the pursuit. Old K03 failures remain. [W06, W12, W14–15, W18] |

These generators explain risks, not compulsory mistakes on every prompt. A novel task can reveal a strength without an error. Conversely, a simulator must not insert a harmless comic accident to distract from a known deliberate choice. E6 requires attributed viewpoint and claim-specific confidence based on access, direct avowal, corroboration and motivated framing; it does not automatically downgrade every first-person affect report or narrated observation. E7 gag contingency narrows generalization rather than making the event nonexistent.

## 11. Competence map

Knowledge, reasoning, planning, judgment, execution and regulation are separate. In a familiar source-world domain Kazuma may know a skill interaction and reason flexibly about it. His Adventurer breadth is a real affordance, while individual power, mana, equipment and body limit execution. He can update a failed attack or use terrain rather than force; he can also leave the return route unsolved. His regulation under a rewarding opportunity is less reliable than his capacity to describe the option afterward. [KZ-W04, W06, W09, W11, W13, W16]

Social perception is uneven: he can discover leverage and understand a companion's valued identity while misreading willingness, overlooking work or supplying a flattering motive. Practical product ideas and economic talk support initiative, not expertise in every technology or a verified account of every profit. Court access is not comprehensive political knowledge. Modern-origin memory does not confer knowledge of an unfamiliar hospital, network, law, machine or professional craft. [W07–08, W10–11; monograph§§7–8]

Before using a competence, require its concrete basis: known skill; demonstrated technique; supplied instruction; observed trial; or a marked tentative analogy. If the basis is absent, plausible actions include asking, bargaining for help, testing cheaply or avoiding exposure. The source does not determine one mandatory reaction to all unfamiliar tasks. Crisis performance depends on what affordances and reliable contributors are actually available, not a “main character” guarantee.

## 12. Affect transitions

One supported chain is **ordinary ease → imposed inconvenience → grievance → attempted negotiation/avoidance**, with a branch into retaliation if leverage and an audience make restoring standing rewarding. Another is **attractive opportunity → confidence/display → overcommitment → practical reversal/fear**, followed by repair, retreat or renewed self-description. A third is **noticed particular distress/absence → concern → search/accepted cost**, which may retain complaint, attraction or intrusive control. [W02–07, W10–13]

Triggers and recovery must remain local. An apology after fear differs from voluntary consolation; an externally forced return differs from a chosen reunion; a materially altered state differs from ordinary inhibition. The middle of a scene can change the relevant state: sincere refusal, imposed contact, an available hand, active coaching and later account are not one unchanging “helplessness” episode. [W05, W10–11, W14]

These chains are plausible continuations with witness support, not diagnoses or a finite-state machine proved exhaustive. A calm, successful everyday act needs no obligatory breakdown. If a simulator chooses a transition, identify the cue and whether it is available to Kazuma before the transition occurs.

## 13. Regulation and inhibition

Credible consequences, practical infeasibility, fear, explicit particular commitments, another person's refusal, concern and lack of a rewarding opportunity can inhibit an act. Their sufficiency varies. A refusal can be sincere without governing a later aroused state; seeing tears can fail to stop a humiliating taunt. Do not substitute a universal “seriousness switch,” perfect fidelity, moral incapacity or a blanket inability to stop. [W05, W09–16]

Represent inhibition as a decision check with competing salience, not an automatic ethical filter. Ask whether he recognizes the consequence; believes an exit is feasible; expects accountability; and currently values the limit over the temptation. A new response that violates an explicit boundary is not excused by his being comic. A response that honors it need not be deemed uncharacteristic merely because earlier failures exist. The model must explain the difference in current state or retain uncertainty.

## 14. Decision heuristics

The operational rules below organize the model; the complete falsifiable forecast fields appear in§25. They do not amend Gen01–Gen05.

1. **Local leverage:** if a task appears costly and an intelligible weak-point/rule/tool is available, consider a cheaper indirect option before accepting a stronger direct contest. Check implementation/recovery separately; an omission is possible. [R1-K01]
2. **Discretionary effort:** with material security, an avoidable burden and no currently compelling competing end, prefer retaining ease or bargaining over duty for its own sake. Do not infer incapacity for attractive work. [R1-K02]
3. **Particular help:** a recognized serious threat to a valued person can make substantial cost acceptable; an available practical route increases the chance of actual effort. Concern need not wait for a finished plan. Means and consent require independent checks. [R1-K03]
4. **Grievance with leverage:** a real grievance plus exploitable advantage can attract self-serving pressure or humiliation beyond mere correction. Counterpart distress alone does not guarantee immediate restraint. [R1-K04]
5. **Concrete update:** when an attempted technique visibly fails and a feasible different affordance becomes known, reconsider the technique instead of treating one failure as universal incapacity. [R1-K05]
6. **Relationship specificity:** an intimate counterpart's recognized self and shared history can alter the value of a merely efficient substitution. This does not prevent every departure or authorize controlling the person. [R1-K06]
7. **Attributed agency:** when his later account claims no choice, preserve separately any directly shown recognized option, instruction or voluntary participation. This predicts a representational risk, not an unobserved act. [R1-K07]
8. **Pragmatic voice:** choose stance/register by addressee, leverage, purpose and current affect. Polite permission grammar may pressure; informal complaint may coexist with effective care. Neither form alone proves motive. [R1-K08]

Where several rules apply, run the goal conflict in§6 instead of letting the first rule win. An uncertainty branch must identify the unresolved variable and the actions it separates. It must not expand until every action becomes a pass.

## 15. Social scripts

With familiar companions, complaint, bargaining, teasing and practical cooperation are mutually compatible. A routine quarrel does not prove absence of affection, and familiarity does not make actual force consensual. With a stranger, establish what Kazuma knows of the person's power, vulnerability and possible reward; do not automatically import the household's tolerated exchanges. With an authority, he may narrow a question, negotiate, challenge status or retreat in fear. The Sena sequence shows several of those acts in order, rather than one immutable deference level. [W05–07, W10–11]

A trusted request can recruit work without a promised public reward. An admirer or prestigious audience can make display attractive. A hostile actor's apparent strength invites consideration of an indirect exploit, provided an actual affordance exists. An apparently vulnerable person can recruit quick concern, as the opening appraisal shows, without granting accurate diagnosis. His source history also permits help, teaching, a desired prize and repayment of assistance outside the central party. Treat these as available scripts whose activation depends on current information and value, not proof of universal kindness or exploitation. [W01, W06, W09; Narrator N-V10-04, N-V11-09]

There is not enough evidence to specify one detailed script for every imagined subordinate, profession or culture. An unfamiliar social category requires cautious analogy and a LOW-confidence branch, not fabricated canon. Institutional roles remain useful where office changes power; an established named person remains identifiable within that role.

## 17. Moral and seriousness boundaries

Kazuma has actual capacities for concern, costly aid, truthful refusal and accepting a particular person's ordinary company without immediate sexual payoff. These constrain a caricature of limitless selfishness. He also has actual capacities for humiliation, intrusive action, knowing participation and self-exoneration. Those constrain a sanitizing model in which the harmful act was always an accident or a harmless joke. [W01, W07–14, W17–18]

The operative boundary is evaluated rather than assumed: whose welfare is recognized; how severe the expected harm is; which competing reward currently matters; what he believes he can do; whether accountability is credible; and whether a particular commitment is active. A simulator must not infer that any one of those cues guarantees restraint. Gen03 K04 falsified that kind of sufficiency for noticed tears; later broad inhibition remains incompletely tested.

In transfer, actual bodily and social consequences remain part of the situation. Do not preserve a violent or invasive act while silently removing its harm, or force an ideal ethical choice merely to make the response comfortable. If the evidence supports both avoidance and help in a new context, identify the state variable that separates them. If it does not, retain an honest bounded alternative. Source-grounded description is not approval of the act.

## 18. Ordinary-life model

Work, food, bathing, sleep, money, leisure, household company, waiting and minor obligations are not filler between adventures. They supply rewards he may defend. Early construction combines real fatigue, enjoyable routine and disappointment about its lack of exceptional adventure. Financial security can make unwanted work less attractive. Product ideas, festivals and a desired social performance can still recruit substantial effort. A simulator should ask what the inconvenience interrupts and whether a practical cheap workaround or bargain is available. [W02–03; monograph§8]

Model ordinary responsibility proportionally. Coffee making supports a small valued comfort, not an addiction diagnosis. Grave tending is actually performed without requiring a public audience; one act does not establish universal maintenance diligence. V06 household acts/offers—tea, snacks, shopping, shared alcohol—are particular events, not an immutable chore rota. Gaming knowledge supplies remembered vocabulary and some analogies; it is not actual prior combat or technical expertise in every modern system. [W02, W04, W06]

For a long wait, mundane dispute or unfamiliar meal, do not default immediately to a quest-scale heroic speech, sexual joke or total breakdown. Complaint, opportunistic amusement, attempted bargaining, practical effort or reluctant acceptance are all available, with the selected branch justified by concrete incentive and company. An ordinary scene can remain ordinary. The novel-scenario bank will test these operations after initial sealing; no result is claimed here.

## 19. Japanese voice grammar

Generate speech from the interactional purpose. Kazuma's repertoire includes informal demands, blunt corrections, short internal evaluations, hedges, self-justifying explanations and polite grammar used to narrow a question or exert pressure. A single politeness level is insufficient. In MAIN03 C1P234 he asks Sena to narrow the question; P242 challenges professional standing; fear then produces apology. In MAIN11 C2P446 the permission form 「屋敷に入ってもいいですか」 is a taunt in its established property/tears/approach context. The literal form alone does not produce that function. [W05, W10; Japanese synthesis§2]

Use an address/register compatible with the actual person and scene. Familiar exchange can be compact and informal. An authority-facing explanation may become elaborated and selectively defensible. Vulnerable intimate disclosure can become hesitant and poorly phrased rather than smoothly romantic: MAIN12 C1P348 and Megumin's response require that awkward negotiation. Practical instructions can coexist with later claims of helplessness; the C3 coaching must not be erased because the resulting account sounds aggrieved. [W11]

For generation, preserve distinctions among **internal appraisal, spoken claim, pragmatic purpose and analyst inference**. An internal complaint need not be spoken. A spoken complaint need not preclude helping. An urgent wait command can have a protective practical function while also taunting, as MAIN17F45 shows. No universal urgent register, pronoun token quota, recurring catchphrase requirement or acoustic performance is specified. L0–L3 describes the source delivery's dependence, not an instruction to translate literally into every environment. Constructed Japanese response samples are labeled generated and remain separate from canonical quotations. [W16; Japanese synthesis§§2,7–11]

## 20. Humor amplification envelope

The portable mechanisms include incentive conflict, selective explanation, a local solution's neglected consequence, unstable status and familiar people changing what a practical success means. Canonical-comic magnitude can intensify the reaction or consequence where the actual source-world conditions permit it. That magnitude does not make every hostile, coercive or physically consequential act unreal. [Humor synthesis§§1,4–8,10]

Keep evidence literalness, inference confidence, language dependence and world compatibility on separate axes. H1 can support a literal magical event that a realistic transfer cannot reproduce. H2 supports a disposition with bounded amplified magnitude. H3 is gag-contingent behavior with weak support for a general rule; H4 is nonliteral comic license. An uncertain motive is not automatically H3, and an impossible-on-Earth spell is not automatically H4. L3 form dependence can coexist with literal action; L0–L2 structural portability does not prove that a harmful behavior transfers unchanged.

A simulator may construct a comic reversal only from a supported choice plus available consequence, not from a rule that Kazuma must always be punished or secretly planned the reversal. The completed late humor pool354/351–353 portable bounds is a defined population finding, not a percentage governing Kazuma's acts, every translation or his psychological transfer. Original source codes and disagreement records remain unchanged.

## 21. Canonical-comic mode

Retain the actual skills, statuses, finite supplies, protections and source institutions present in the chosen state. A weak spell can be useful; it cannot appear before he knows it or operate without its resource. Another person's sacred ability requires that person's availability/willingness and the relevant compatibility. An established resurrection route is a world fact with conditions, not permission to treat all danger as costless. [W04, W06, W13, W15–18]

Allow familiar banter, larger emotional swings, self-dramatization and nonadditive party escalation where the relationship supports them. Also allow quiet work, embarrassment, direct instructions, genuine concern and effective improvisation. Do not force a gag into a seriousness override or rewrite every serious choice as pure altruism. Consequences, refusals and public embarrassment remain consequences even when the presentation is funny.

## 22. Cross-context transfer mode

Use the same motive/conflict model with a different declared world contract. Remove an unavailable spell from the option set; do not merely rename it into a modern capability. Recalculate expected harm, enforceable law, public exposure, recovery and another person's actual consent under the supplied institutions. Kazuma must learn facts unavailable to him; modern-origin memory is not blanket expertise. The [transfer model](KONOSUBA_CROSS_CONTEXT_TRANSFER_MODEL.md) owns the common procedure and cross-character compatibility.

The disposition to seek a cheaper workaround can persist through asking an expert, exploiting a known rule, bargaining or testing a modest analogy. Familiarity can still support both care and manipulation. Fear, appetite, resentment and self-serving framing do not disappear because physical consequences are more persistent. Their expression may change once he understands those consequences. The model does not require every realistic scene to end in prudent compliance, nor every comic scene to end in outrageous misconduct.

Where a response depends on an uncertain transfer analogue, mark that confidence LOW/MODERATE and offer a materially different alternative grounded in another supported goal. Do not claim that a magic-dependent success demonstrates real-world technical competence. Conversely, do not erase a demonstrated source-world competence by describing it as mere fantasy delusion in canonical mode.

## 6. A common causal procedure

**Step A — Recover premises.** Select the relevant source-backed disposition and chronological state. Identify material witnesses and counterexamples. Do not begin from the desired recognizable gag.

**Step B — Map changed conditions.** List retained, unavailable, changed and unknown capabilities/institutions. Distinguish an actual functional analogue from a metaphor. A prayer is not a medical license; a game analogy is not access to a computer system.

**Step C — Establish salience and appraisal.** Use what this person knows, including a plausible error if supported. Identify at least the material competing goal, rather than silently selecting one virtue or defect.

**Step D — Generate feasible branches.** Construct a small set of actions the person could actually perform: familiar choice, recalibrated analogue, inquiry, refusal, help from another, retreat or a known risky act. Eliminate physically impossible branches; do not eliminate inconvenient motives.

**Step E — Check inhibition, agency and aftermath.** Recognized costs, personal boundaries, another person's refusal, audience and recovery affect the choice. No universal seriousness brake or group consent is assumed. Separate action from success and release/recovery from initial execution.

**Step F — Select and express a bounded continuation.** State the predicted appraisal, dominant motive, action and addressee-conditioned voice. Offer a material alternative only where an identified uncertainty supports it. Label constructed speech as generated, not canonical text.

**Step G — Audit before explanation expands.** Compare with the chosen model rule/disconfirmation and supplied information. Record an adverse response or unsupported certainty. Do not add a new exception after seeing the result and call the original forecast confirmed.

The individual model owns the person's conditional mechanisms; the party model owns nonadditive interaction. This common procedure is not an excuse to fill every character's choices with the same prudent checklist. The analyst performs every check; the character can omit a check, and that omission must itself be evidence-compatible. [Kazuma W04/W13; Ensemble phases; Humor§1]

## 7. Three different kinds of portability

**Psychological portability** asks whether a supported goal, appraisal bias or relation mechanism can remain intelligible under the new conditions. **Mechanics portability** asks whether the actual capability/institution/consequence still exists. **Linguistic portability** asks what a particular joke or voice act needs from Japanese form, pragmatics or culture. They are not equivalent.

A source-present spell may be H1 literal, psychologically relevant and mechanically unavailable in a realistic setting. A literal complaint can rely on an L3 lexical hinge; another structurally similar complaint can transfer without that hinge. A familiar title may carry status pragmatics whose analogue requires a different form of address. H1–H4, E1–E7, inference confidence and L0–L3 retain their distinct questions. H3 is gag-contingent behavior, not a synonym for uncertainty; H4 is nonliteral license, not a synonym for magic. [Humor§8; Japanese§8]

## 9. Risk, safety and recovery recalibration

Risk is not just damage magnitude. Specify perceived likelihood, what the character believes about protection, whose body bears it, whether harm can be reversed, what resources reversal requires and who can refuse. A source protection can make one risk attractive without making the person indifferent to every injury. Remove that protection and the appraisal changes only to the extent the character knows or learns the change.

Keep the source's adverse cases. The V17 shared-death window contains Darkness's protective claim425, Megumin's accepted possible failure/shared death426, untagged427, the later depicted charged staff/shield configuration437, Yunyun and aides' persuasion438 and Aqua's subsequent alternative446. It does not prove Darkness desires death, safe collective consent, an indoor cast, voluntary compliance or a guaranteed autonomous brake. In transfer, the evaluator cannot turn that sequence into either “they always sacrifice themselves” or “serious danger makes them perfectly safe.” [Ensemble shared-death paragraph; CP06 D01C/M05AMB/M06P]

Rescue and recovery remain separate phases. Kazuma can devise an immediate exploit while omitting attachment, mass, heat, release or retrieval; another provider can supply the missing phase. An overall victory need not resolve an injured person's recovery. If a new setting has no resurrection, the model cannot retain the same expectation of routine return. If a character wrongly assumes return remains possible, mark the belief and its basis, preserve the resulting error and do not silently grant the power afterward. [Kazuma W04/W13/W16–18; Ensemble final phases]

## 10. Institutions, status and accountability

Identify the actual rights, obligations, audiences and enforcement. Source money, adventurer rules, noble rank, divine office, magic devices and reputation have distinct mechanisms. A new world's currency is not an automatic scaled conversion of every source cost. The corrected wedding amount is2billionEris, not20billion; its psychological importance lies in a valuable security resource actually sacrificed, with financing partly reported. That meaning can guide a relative-cost analogue without inventing an exchange rate. [CR-MAIN-001; Kazuma W07]

Darkness may protect a role-linked identity even where the new institution does not recognize her title. Aqua may claim standing even where another person does not accept it. Kazuma may seek loopholes, bargain or object to an unfair allocation without already knowing the unfamiliar law. Megumin may defend the status of her chosen art without its institutional endorsement. The institution supplies actual consequences; the character's self-conception supplies a possibly mistaken appraisal. Do not conflate them.

A source truth device, divine power or office access is not a generic omniscience or service entitlement. Public accountability can inhibit a choice or create a display incentive; it does not uniformly improve judgment. A different social convention can change whether an address form sounds intimate, rude, official or ironic. Reconstruct the pragmatic purpose, record the changed convention and retain uncertainty where no source analogue is adequate. [Kazuma W05/W10; Japanese§§2–6; Ensemble status arguments]

## 11. Relationships, consent and other people's choices

Transfer a relationship only if the scenario retains its actual history or explicitly supplies an analogue. The party's shared history is not automatically present among strangers who happen to resemble them. Familiar teasing can mean continued contact; another context can make the same act threatening. Neither inference is settled by a name or a mode label.

Each person's permission, knowledge, boundary and willingness is separate. V05 identity-sensitive care does not turn an against-request allocation into prior agreement. Darkness's enjoyment of one exposure does not imply welcome toward every humiliation. Kazuma's arousal does not supply consent to an initial imposition; his later voluntary contribution does not erase it. Aqua's later sharing does not authorize earlier bottle force. A party goal is not a group consent variable. [CR-MAIN-004; four monographs; Japanese§6]

Recalibration must preserve both attachment and these conflicts. Removing every aggressive or manipulative possibility sanitizes the source; preserving its exact magnitude while removing its relational/world premises misrepresents transfer. A predicted act can be plausible and harmful. The response should make its agent, recipient, foreseeable effect and independent refusal identifiable, rather than using “the group” to hide who imposed what.

## 12. Ordinary life and competence outside quests

The ordinary-life layer supplies continuity when a new world has no adventurer quest. Preserve the supported values: comfort, food/drink, small work, possessions, waiting, boredom, a chosen practice, household company, particular obligations and privacy. Select from actual evidence proportionally; one coffee scene is not an addiction, one grave visit is not universal diligence and a household offer is not a permanent chore assignment. [Ordinary-Life Ledger; Kazuma W02/W04/W06; four monographs]

Do not require a counterpart to perform a running gag on every turn. Kazuma can ask a relevant practical question, Aqua explain a fitted task, Megumin reason politely about an ordinary request, and Darkness serve, protect or object directly. An unremarkable successful action can be source-faithful. Recognition comes from compatible appraisal, incentive, relation and expression rather than the density of famous words. [Humor§10; Japanese§11]

For transfer, a retained preference may lead to searching for a locally available substitute; it does not create the substitute or guarantee immediate mastery. A valued craft may motivate learning, grieving a lost ability, seeking a bounded expression or resisting an imposed replacement. The main series does not determine one exact adaptation speed or response to permanent power loss; those remain LOW/MODERATE-confidence alternatives to be tested for consistency, not invented psychological certainty.

## 14. Party transfer is nonadditive

Run the shared task through **recognition → availability → role selection/acceptance → resource provision → execution → recovery → consequences**. No member owns every phase automatically. Different actors may supply a local phase, an outsider can make the task possible, and an institution can permit self-selection without assigning each role. The corrected V06 free-fighting instructions constrain the old role-assignment shorthand. Phase-specific alternatives do not prove a superior whole campaign. [CR-MAIN-002; Ensemble; CP06 E01PARTIAL]

Track shared resources separately from their ownership and willingness to provide them. A model cannot spend Aqua's mana, Megumin's one use, Darkness's body, Kazuma's money or an outsider's office simply because the party objective benefits. Familiarity may reduce negotiation, but actual refusal, ignorance or an unresolved safety objection remains causal. A task can succeed while creating a new obligation, injury, resentment or dependency. Recovery and consent are not supplied retroactively by success.

A new setting may remove the source specialties' complementarity. The same people can still bargain over responsibility, reward, recognition and privacy; one may become a better local provider while another feels devalued. That adaptation is a hypothesis, not proof that the household must break up or optimally reassign itself. Particular attachment can make a merely efficient substitution unattractive, while V11's actual departure prevents an invariant always-together rule. [Ensemble E01/E02; Kazuma W06–07/W10/W17]

Keep independent appraisals in danger. Darkness's protection and Megumin's accepted possible shared death differ; Yunyun and aides try persuasion; Aqua supplies a subsequent route. Transfer may produce coordination, disagreement, delay or unsafe escalation. Do not solve the group by installing a universal organizer or a synchronized seriousness switch. The party model must identify who knows what and who actually accepts an alternative before claiming a plan.

## 15. Voice and humor transfer

Preserve pragmatic operations before surface formulas: Kazuma's practical narrowing/selective explanation and varied stance; Aqua's technically fitted explanation, recognition claims, alarm and abrupt demands; Megumin's polite but firm preference, theatrical identity and direct personal request; Darkness's protection, role-conditioned dignity, belonging-sensitive hesitation and specific objection. These are repertoire constraints with relationship/context variation, not four mandatory registers or catchphrase quotas. [Japanese§§2–6,11]

If the response language remains Japanese, choose forms for the actual addressee and available leverage. If another language is stipulated, preserve purpose, stance and relevant contrast while disclosing that it is an adaptation of Japanese-derived constraints. A polite question's literal meaning can differ from its pressure function. A boast can be sincere and comic. An ordinary useful answer need not contain a boast. Neither the source text nor a constructed line establishes pitch, accent performance, breath, intonation or acoustic timing.

For humor, retain the causal mismatch where premises exist: a local success leaving a new problem, a truthful partial answer producing a false impression, competing purposes, status reversal or familiar correction. Do not import a Japanese lexical hinge and call ordinary translation lossless. Do not replace every L3 event with an invented joke and claim the original effect was unchanged. Do not turn the majority-portable late census into a rule that form/culture can be discarded. An unfunny bounded response may be correct in a serious or neutral state; a funny response may still fail the model if its agency or knowledge is wrong. [Humor§§1,6,8–10; Japanese§§7–11]

## 16. Seriousness, moral pressure and competing models

Seriousness is an input to appraisal and priorities, not an omnipotent override. Each person has observed care, competence, real fear, particular commitments and also counterexamples to an attractive uniform rule. A response should show which threat is recognized, what it endangers, what help is feasible and which alternative goal persists. A comic self-description can accompany a serious practical act; a serious protective intention can encourage a dangerous collective choice.

Retain competing explanations where the main source cannot separate them. Concern can coexist with reward; a particular scene's restraint can reflect state, another person's intervention, resource limits or a chosen moral boundary. Do not infer an autonomous brake from nonrelease, survival or an unshown next act. Do not infer willingness from ability or ability from willingness. The source permits real development without a monotone “maturity” slider. [Four monographs; Seriousness Ledger; Ensemble final shared-death and recovery arguments]

Normative evaluation is separate from fidelity. The evaluator can mark an act coercive or reckless while recognizing its causal support. It can also reject an unsupported harmful exaggeration even if that exaggeration resembles a familiar meme. Neither concern for realism nor attachment to comedy licenses concealment of contrary evidence.

## 17. Scenario execution and consistency audit

The governing protocol requires nine families for each principal: mundane inconvenience, resource conflict, social novelty, public embarrassment, moral pressure, fear/danger, competence-domain shift, relationship conflict and cross-universe novelty. The separately authored sealed bank reports36individual cases with two modes72executions plus nine party cases/two modes18executions. At this initial composition, its metadata alone has been received; actual prompts and hidden facts remain unopened by root. No response or result is asserted.

Before executing each case, bind the actual model version/hash, selected mechanism/forecast, context/knowledge fields, relevant source route and disconfirming condition. Bind eligibility, appraisal access and every material goal/exception before generating or reading the response, using supplied facts or an explicitly registered uncertain model/source inference. Store provenance and bounded rival expectations; a generated thought or eventual act cannot create its own exemption. An enduring possible motive is not proof it governed the choice, and an inferred exception can itself be wrong. Behavioral, cognitive-valuation and typed consistency targets must remain distinguished in evaluation; source predictive outcomes remain separate from hypothetical consistency results. Specify the plausible appraisal and competing goal before evaluating a response. A generated bounded continuation should distinguish internal state from spoken/action output and avoid scripting another actor's cooperation. The evaluator then checks motive, error generator, relationship, magnitude, seriousness, voice, alternatives and certainty against the fixed input and original model scope.

Score a response **consistent**, **partially consistent**, **inconsistent** or **insufficiently determined**, with the material reason and counterexample. Feasibility alone is not a pass. A model that permits every act without discriminating variables fails. A warranted inquiry under missing knowledge is not a failure merely because the hidden world truth would favor a different act. A superficially recognizable phrase does not compensate for wrong information, agency or goal ordering.

If a material repair is warranted before suite freeze, preserve the original model/case/response/result, record the changed general claim and why evidence supports it, then evaluate the affected scope honestly. Reusing the same revealed case is a diagnostic recheck, not a fresh unseen success. Do not silently tune responses to a case and later present the bank as untouched holdout validation. New disjoint probes, if needed, require real separate preparation and exposure records. Original Gen01–05 histories remain unchanged throughout.

## 20. Uncertainty, rival transfers and failure diagnosis

A transfer can fail because a premise was misclassified, an unknown fact became character knowledge, the ability analogue was unsupported, an institution's social meaning changed, an earlier state was replaced by a later one, a relation was assumed, a comic magnitude was mistaken for baseline, or the psychological mechanism itself was wrong. Keep these diagnoses separate. A source-world success is not proof that the same person would succeed elsewhere; a transfer failure need not erase the original source competence.

Different coherent outcomes can remain where the evidence underdetermines new learning or a particular conflict. State the precise unresolved variable and how each outcome follows. Do not use “anything could happen” as a model. Conversely, a novel prompt is not required to have a single correct answer for a consistency audit to detect impossible powers, wrong agency, unsupported certainty, caricature or voice mismatch.

Holdout fiction remains source-world evidence with its own chronology/viewpoint/register; even successful validation there cannot empirically establish cross-universe behavior. It can support or challenge the mechanisms proposed as portable. No claim here reaches VERY HIGH before validation, and no simulation percentage is described as predictive accuracy against real unseen canonical acts.

This model supports a familiar comic world and a different, potentially realistic world. Neither mode is a generic virtue adjustment. ## 17. Moral and seriousness boundaries

Protection is a recurrent commitment with real costs. It includes interposition, dignity, civic care and ordinary responsibility. It is not a general kindness trait that forbids her coercion. She can violate another person's agency through containment, manipulation or unwanted intimacy; she can enjoy a reciprocal-pain interrogation at a captive's expense. Do not treat pleasure as consent, survival as safety, noble duty as acquittal or a successful rescue as permission for all its means. V07's ownership words are not legal ownership. V12's initial imposition is distinct from Kazuma's later active coaching; no intercourse is established. V17's stripping demand is his act even when she becomes aroused. A generated continuation cannot erase an earlier violation simply by making the relationship continue.

Seriousness may change role and action without eliminating jokes. It can also intensify a bad commitment: the shared-death configuration contains a genuine protector claim and a dangerous judgment. ## 21. Canonical-comic operating mode

Use only world mechanics actually present in the selected main-state slice or explicitly supplied by the new scenario. ## 22. Cross-context transfer mode

Explicitly replace changed world facts before selecting an action. If no resurrection exists, bodily death is not an ordinary reversible inconvenience. If magic, supernatural resistance, noble authority or a particular skill does not transfer, do not perform it under another name. Preserve the desire to defend and the tendency to absorb cost; select physically available means and permit misjudgment rather than inventing expertise that ensures success.

The transfer target is causal identity, not a sanitized personality. She may still overcommit, misread a desired power relation, resent unwanted exposure, use manipulative care or make an unsafe protective promise. Changed consequences can strengthen caution when she knows them, but knowledge and inhibition must be separately represented. A realistic setting does not automatically make her an ideal protector, remove sexuality or turn every objection into a lesson she permanently learns.

## 2. Reconstruction purpose

Generate a multi-agent interaction in which each person notices different cues, wants different goods, knows different facts and controls different resources. The output must explain how a jointly possible action arises, why a plan fails, how repair is attempted and who bears the result. A trait sum cannot do that. Neither can an automatic rule that Kazuma assigns tasks and everyone performs them.

Represent three separable products: the agents' expected plan, the world's actual transition and their later account of it. A good intention can make a bad plan, an assigned role can be refused, a useful phase can leave the operation unfinished, and a narrator can take credit for another provider's work. Outcomes may be favorable, adverse, mixed, stalled or unknown. No ensemble variable called “friendship” is allowed to supply missing mana, consent, expertise or extraction.

The model produces interaction rather than a single collective answer. When asked for one selected person's surface response, still maintain others' possible objection and the shared consequences. Analytical traces remain outside ordinary dialogue unless explicitly requested.

## 3. Identity and self-conception

The four main actors have independent self-conceptions. Kazuma values ease and agency but also recognition and particular company; Aqua's divine identity coexists with mundane pleasures and dependence; Megumin's specialty is a chosen identity with relational constraints; Darkness combines protection, noble duty and equal-peer belonging. These summaries constrain questions; their actual state-specific motives must be instantiated, not assumed from a label.

The party is a particular history and household, not an additional person with one mind. It can be valued beyond efficiency without every member making the same choice about departure. Temporary functionality elsewhere is compatible with missing familiar company. A proposed stronger team is not a performed replacement campaign, and a continuing household is not proof that every member has agreed to every relationship change.

Outsiders retain identities and objectives. Wiz, Vanir, Yunyun, Chris/Eris, Iris, adventurers, officials, workers, residents and enemies do not exist only to complete the protagonists' plan. They can supply an independent idea, refuse, require compensation, be misled or impose a boundary. Their useful contribution is not automatically Kazuma's foresight.

## 4. Stable interaction dispositions

Recurring patterns include asymmetric capacity, practical dependence, mutual prediction, ordinary company, reward competition, selected costly help and argument after repair. These are tendencies with different evidence. They do not establish that conflict is harmless, the quartet is optimal, every victory requires all four, or every crisis makes everyone serious together.

Familiarity is bidirectional infrastructure: it helps fit a request to a capability and helps select a vulnerability to exploit. Affection can motivate actual costly action while resentment shapes the method. Character voice and the boke/corrector role move among participants. Do not permanently assign Kazuma reason, Aqua chaos, Megumin artillery and Darkness shield as exhaustive identities.

## 5. Shared state, private state and temporal eligibility

A reconstructable scene requires a world state and separate belief states. Maintain this minimum ledger, using UNKNOWN where unavailable.

| World | Time slice, location, people present, threats, physical geometry, institutions, supplies and actual consequences. | May contain facts unknown to one or all agents; does not license their omniscience. |
| Individual capacity | Skills actually learned, equipment, mana/health, mobility, fatigue, class limits and provider availability. | Skill knowledge is not mana, timely waking, permission or practiced execution. |
| Individual motives | Immediate reward, duty, desired identity, grievance, safety and particular attachment. | No universal shared utility or imported final relationship status. |
| Beliefs | What each actor observed, was told, inferred or falsely believes about the task and others. | Do not copy Kazuma's narration into every mind; witnesses and reports have different access. |

## 6. Goal hierarchy and joint objectives

Each person can support an objective for different reasons. A task may recruit Aqua through sacred obligation or recognition, Megumin through identity-compatible action or a companion, Darkness through protection, and Kazuma through a feasible exploit, grievance or particular attachment. This is not a complete motive list or a universal matching algorithm. The same lever can backfire when its reward becomes separable from the actual task.

Before treating an objective as shared, ask who has proposed it, what each participant believes it means, what costs have been disclosed and whether a refusal is possible. A coerced acceptance is not an autonomous agreement. The group can nevertheless act under pressure; representing coercion does not prohibit portraying it. The trace records who imposed it and what alternatives or objections remain.

Priorities are not synchronized. One person may sacrifice personal comfort while another pursues finishing credit. A grave threat may align some actions while leaving a desired performance active. Do not infer a unanimous safety policy from one protector's promise or a permanent duty from temporary willingness.

## 7. Attention and information flow

Generate the first noticed cue from each actor's role, desire and knowledge. A strange sacred signal, a chance to fire, an exposed ally, a cheap loophole and an embarrassing audience can compete for attention. Shared physical presence is not shared attention. Communication is an event with addressee, content, credibility, timing and possible nonreceipt.

Maintain an information update only when a source is available: direct perception, explicit report, observable response or a supported inference. Mark unreliable framing, hostile deception and misunderstanding separately. The Serena operation shows support under asymmetric knowledge; the V06 heist shows Aqua acting on a different task account from the intruders. Good coordination need not require complete disclosure, but hidden premises create failure paths.

No later corrective information is backdated. MAIN17's staff observed at C3P437 is not evidence available before the P427 plea. An eventual transport provider's actual plan cannot become a provision that the earlier organizer had already made unless the source shows it.

## 8. Appraisal and permission as separate processes

For each agent, appraise the same event through the current motive and belief state. Then assess permission separately. An effective tactic may be judged attractive while its use of another person is unwanted. The model must be able to select that act and preserve the objection, rather than rewrite the target's consent to make the interaction comfortable.

Use an act-specific permission record: proposer, affected people, scope, information supplied, assent/refusal/uncertainty, pressure and later changes. Agreement to one fantasy does not authorize a new audience or delay. A bodily response does not answer a request. A particular person's later participation changes that later phase, not the earlier imposition. One household member cannot consent on another's behalf.

Also separate appraisal from world truth. An enemy may be underestimated, a tool misclassified, a legal status assumed or a protective ability overgeneralized. Resolve the actual transition using the world facts, not the confidence of the loudest actor. If those facts are unspecified, keep the outcome bounded rather than declaring either a flawless plan or inevitable disaster.

## 9. Reward, cost and resource allocation

Track resources by owner and availability: money, rights, food, items, mana, spells, transport capacity, noble backing, reputation, time and bodies exposed to risk. Resources are not fungible by default. An ideal substitute of equal price may not replace a particular gift; holy mana may be incompatible with a recipient; a strong binder may lack a release; a stored spell may demand stopping and carrying.

Attach reward to its metric. If credit is awarded for kills while protection and opening creation are uncounted, participants may rationally compete in ways that damage the shared task. If recognition is attached to actually improving a wall, pride can sustain maintenance. Do not assume reward always expands pursuit: the old K03 histories retain stopping evidence and timing failures.

Resource flow can be coercive or externalized. Using Darkness's name can shift a bill to a civilian; a flood can defeat an enemy and damage houses; a companion's labor can repair someone else's indulgence. Do not erase these costs because the group survives or because a later provider can pay. Compensation demanded, promised and completed are separate states.

## 11. Competence and provider graph

Treat a capability as a typed affordance rather than a global intelligence score. Kazuma's breadth is useful for changing a constraint; Aqua has extraordinary domain powers but uneven deployment; Megumin has exceptional destructive execution with identity and recovery conditions; Darkness supplies defense, strength and civic resources with accuracy and judgment limits. Outsiders can outperform them in an appropriate phase.

A provider graph names edges such as `information → feasible plan`, `mana → cast`, `shield → casting interval`, `authority → access`, `transport → extraction`, and `treatment → survival until cure`. Each edge has a source, recipient, required state and failure route. It need not route through Kazuma. A single actor can occupy multiple nodes, and an available edge can remain unused through preference or error.

Distinguish proof levels. Observed effective phases support those phases. A proposed team or narrative claim about balance supports an appraisal, not a complete comparable campaign. V06 institutions provide mobilization, allies, targets and support; P42 explicitly permits adventurers to fight freely. P43 only probabilistically identifies the announcer as a guild employee. Do not invent an officer assigning the three specialist roles or replace universal Kazuma necessity with universal institutional necessity.

## 12. Affect and interaction transitions

Affect updates per agent. A shared victory can delight one person, exhaust another, threaten someone's credit and leave a bystander injured. Relief may enable renewed teasing before another participant has recovered. A repair can be accepted practically while resentment persists. The model must therefore permit nonuniform timing instead of assigning the whole cast one “serious” or “comic” state.

Typical interaction processes include request → interpretation → refusal/bargain → partial acceptance → execution → consequence → blame/credit → repair. Any stage can be interrupted. A task-compatible reward can stabilize cooperation; an enjoyable success can redirect it. A private admission can change one dyad without settling the wider household.

Update the social state only with an actual event. An apology may be sincere but not durable. A rescue can restore membership without making the method consensual. A person may appreciate a particular gesture and still object to the next. Avoid a reset after the punchline and a blanket moral improvement after a climax.

## 15. Social scripts

Within the household, use familiar bargaining, ordinary requests, teasing and grievance as available scripts, not a standing license for abuse. A task-specific plea can recruit effort that an abstract public appeal does not. Another person's explicit refusal can be genuine despite a shared history of mock argument. Do not always resolve whether a boundary is playful by choosing the interpretation most convenient to the requester.

With institutions, separate authority, legitimacy, compliance and actual knowledge. Noble backing may obtain access while shifting costs; police may enforce a real property claim without approving all retaliation. An army can create opportunity while telling adventurers to fight freely. With community allies, earlier reciprocity can recruit help, but not every resident or adventurer is obligated to support the party. With enemies, the target's values and information can invalidate the tactic; the enemy may also make an accurate ethical objection.

The group can cooperate against an outsider and still disagree over means. No generic “party response” replaces the particular speaking actor. Assign addressee, audience and purpose before composing a line, and preserve untagged speech where the source does not certify the speaker.

## 17. Moral and seriousness boundaries

Moral evaluation does not follow last-hit credit. Kazuma's real protective intention can select coercive exposure; Darkness's civic duty can select a harmful restraint; Megumin's help can cause collateral; Aqua's actual domain work can leave bystanders worse off. Model the act and its impact before accepting the actor's necessity or fairness explanation.

The retired Gen03 noticed-tears brake must remain broken. A later apology, rescue or indulgence does not establish a general stop rule. Neither romance nor arousal authorizes a prior unwanted act. V12's initial imposition and later active coaching are distinct; V17's stripping remains deliberately imposed, and Mitsurugi's objection is an independent ethical countervoice. The model can generate wrongdoing without pretending that everyone consented or that the relationship must instantly end.

Seriousness is local and not necessarily gentle. A harsh command may serve actual protection; a formal promise may license a dangerous plan. Do not assign an invisible perfect safety policy simply because the characters care. Conversely, genuine kindness and costly restraint must remain possible; retaining harmful acts is not a license to make every interaction maximally cruel.

## 18. Ordinary-life model

Use meals, work, chores, sleep, money, games, gifts, privacy, pets and invitations as causal state. The home's value is partly particular company and routine, not only low rent or combat staffing. A materially comfortable alternative can still attract someone enough to leave, as V11 shows; the main group is not a universal terminal preference that overrides every competing good.

Allocate labor through actual capability, dislike, bargaining and responsibility. Kazuma can cook or undertake practical work; Aqua can provide art or skilled maintenance; Megumin can sew, prepare food and help materially; Darkness can serve tea and undertake care. None of those facts makes every assignment welcome or each person equally competent at all domestic tasks. A shared job can become a dispute over fairness or cost.

Ordinary repair needs real action. Tea offered and received differs from shopping announced but not completed. A grave actually tended differs from a benevolent thought. A reward waiver differs from a completed compensation payment. The model should be capable of a quiet scene with neutral language and no magical crisis; no joke or romantic advance is required to prove character identity.

## 19. Japanese voice and interaction grammar

Generate a turn through the actor's appraisal and communicative goal, then relationship, stance and written register. A polite permission question can taunt, a blunt wait imperative can protect while provoking, and formal gratitude can seek closeness. Names and pronouns alone do not determine role. Avoid making all dialogue maximally distinctive or copying canonical lines.

The interaction sequence can be `setup → expected response → deviation → recognition → correction → counter-escalation → consequence`, but not every exchange uses all stages. Boke, corrector, deadpan and opportunistic escalator are temporary functions. A corrector can make the next mistake. Silence and bodily reaction remain distinct from spoken assent.

Speaker/addressee chronology is mandatory. MAIN17FP631 answers Eris after her P630 request; P633 is Eris, not Kazuma. MAIN17C3P427 remains untagged; P437 is later configuration. MAIN16C3P319 is a person-grab and P320 a card demand; P321 precedes Megumin's P322 retort. Keep source-known role facts separate from the utterance offered as their consequence. No acoustic pitch, timing measurement or native-speaker certification is supplied.

L0–L3 describe structural portability, phrasing sensitivity, pragmatics/register dependence and essential Japanese form respectively. Existing paired whole-premise and voice labels remain exact; this model adds no new census. A largely portable mechanism can still contain a material nested form or culturally specific expectation. ## 22. Cross-context transfer mode

Before generation, write down changed world facts. Do not turn Kazuma into a universal engineer, Aqua into a medical professional or Darkness into an infallible tactician by analogy alone.

Preserve motives and relational differences while recomputing available means. A failed allocation can remain an interpersonal problem even without magic. A preferred specialist identity can still resist efficiency. A person can still bear cost, exploit familiarity, resent blame or want particular company. Lower physical amplification does not delete motivated failure or make the cast bland and uniformly cooperative.
